Run 2 summed test time 24.4 s > wall time 17.0 s (concurrent files). The harness comment itself says integration files 'may execute concurrently'. Conclusion: test-harness non-determinism (F-DG1-009, Medium, non-mandatory); no access-control defect.

summary: PASS on candidate f0baa87d0163560f (commit 5204179). Every assigned fix verifies on this candidate: F-DG1-007 (register: one 422 transition contract, REQ-S19-004 covers migrations 0001-0008, no residuals) and F-DG1-005/008 (the derived creator-assignment audit entry is localized in Arabic and English, with action, user name, role 'Transformation Lead'/'قائد التحوّل', scope and source, and a real, marked, LTR-isolated fallback for unknown values). The round-2 closures F-DG1-001, 002/105, 003, 004 and 006/207 still hold. The eight DG1-final requirements are complete with existing evidence, and the invariants hold: seven provisional tokens, provisional wordmark, no official Mobily or PMI claim, ar-RTL/en-LTR, bundled fonts with no CDN, Decimal money, Unknown never zero or green, G1-G6 kept separate from DG0-DG7. New finding F-DG1-009 (Medium, non-mandatory): the integration project is non-deterministic. 2 of 3 full runs exited 1: an unhandled 57P01 from the new F-DG1-115 race suite's forced drop, and an a12 false red caused by concurrent files on the shared database, because vitest ignores the project-level fileParallelism:false. Triage shows no product defect (a12 isolated 5/5; domain suites green in every run), but the required check should be made deterministic.
narrative: Product behaviour seen live in this round matches the source principles. Closure is not a status edit (B0014 'Benefits before closure', M0092): it is refused with 422 citing the G6 business approval and leaves no trace. The derived TL assignment gives the creator exactly their own record and no approval power. Missing data reads Unknown. Two cosmetic observations are not raised as findings: a null effective_to reads 'Effective until: None' where the admin catalogue's 'No end' / 'بلا نهاية' would be clearer; and the source assignment shows as an LTR UUID, which is acceptable because an assignment has no name. I triaged the integration flake at length because its failing assertion ('a denied create wrote a row') would be an access-control and integrity defect if real. The isolated reruns, the create handler's single-transaction structure, and the vitest NonProjectOptions evidence together show it is not real. The gate should still not depend on a coin-flip test run.
